chung.Syllabus Name: Giao tiếp liên văn hoá_Intercultural Communication
chung.Time Allocation: Study hours (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 105 hours self-study (including assessment, projects and assignments preparation time).
chung.Description:
Teaching Method: Offline.

< - This course serves as an introduction to the field of intercultural communication, the study of communication processes within and across different cultures and social groups.

< - The course aims to develop English-major students' understanding of the key theories, concepts, approaches and practices of intercultural communication in the contemporary world.

< - Issues covered in the course include intercultural communication as embodied in culture, communication, identity; power, stereotyping, and prejudice; verbal, nonverbal, and rhetorical communication; intercultural competence and conflict, intercultural communication in politics, and intercultural communication in organizations. Throughout the course, students will be encouraged to reflect critically on the ways these issues relate to their personal experiences of cultural differences and communication behaviours.

< - They will be able to apply these theories and practices in case studies with a view to identifying effective communicative strategies in intercultural interactions.

< - This course provides English-major students with the opportunity to learn the theoretical foundations of the discipline as well as practical knowledge and skills to help them become effective and ethical communicator across multiple cultural contexts. >

taiLieu: John R. Baldwin, Robin R. Means Coleman, Alberto González, and Suchitra Shenoy-Packer
Introducing Intercultural Communication: Global Cultures and Contexts
Shuang Liu, Zala Volčič, and Cindy Gallois
clo: Understand the brief history of, rationale for, and ethical considerations related to intercultural communication as a field of study, practice, and research.
Describe and analyse the key elements of intercultural communication, such as culture and identity; critically examine identity politics as well as prejudice and intolerance.
Understand the different channels of production and consumption of messages in intercultural communication: verbal, nonverbal, rhetorical, and mediated.

Consider the different intercultural contexts in which the channels of messages are used, as well as associated challenges: cross-cultural adjustment, relationships and conflict, politics, and organizations.
Critically examine the practical applications of the key concepts related to intercultural communication through analysis of real-life case studies.
danhGia:
Suggested Assignment Activity:
'Students work individually to prepare (at home) and deliver (in class) a presentation in the form of mind map/diagram of their various identities and how these relate to their culture(s) and communication patterns.

Students will be encouraged to use any creative thinking or design skills to make the mind map or diagram.

I personally believe that these Assignments are quite manageable and not too overwhelming for students as they will be simple (pre-prepared) individual presentations or in-class group tasks on topics which are entirely part of the chapters under study. I have now amended this to be 'Suggested Assignment Activity' so that individual lecturers may use their discretion as to what tasks to give their students, should they feel that these tasks are too much. However, I do think that these small assignments will be necessary to help students apply the theory learned in class (while Progress Tests will be more for testing their understanding of the different concepts).

Suggested Assignment Activity:
Students work (in class) in groups of 3-4 to come up with an 'advice column' to Vietnamese students who are due to study abroad in a country of their choice. The column will offer suggestions on how to mitigate culture shock and improve cultural adaptation.

Instructor may choose to ask students to present the work in written format for marking, or to present it verbally in class.

Students work in groups of 3 to examine a specific real-life case study related to one of the four themes studied in Part 3 (Intercultural communication competence; Relationships and conflict; Politics and culture; and Intercultural communication in organizations). They need to analyse the different aspects of the theme as illustrated by the case and critically examine the relevance (or lack thereof) of the case to their personal understanding and practice of intercultural communication.
The projects will be formally reviewed by instructor in class (last slot) and feedback provided before the final exam.

Welcome and Course Introduction

This course depends on the active engagement and informed participation of each student. We will use a seminar format where each student is expected to read the material assigned prior to the class meeting, and to join in any activities, discussions, or presentations related to the material.
